subject: computer-science
title: Computer Systems: Stretch — Performance
welcome_lead: What actually makes a computer feel fast? Let's dig.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science stretch adventure on CPU performance: clock speed, cores and cache.
final_note: You can now reason about why one computer outperforms another.

concepts.def: Cycles per second a CPU runs at, in Hertz.
Gigahertz — one billion cycles per second.
An independent processing unit inside a CPU.
CPU with two or more cores that work in parallel.
Data needed is found in the cache — very fast.
Data must be fetched from RAM — much slower.

walkthroughs.body_html: A 3 GHz CPU runs 3,000,000,000 cycles per second. Higher clock = more instructions per second, but also more heat. Cooling and power become limits.
Two cores can run two threads at once. A 4-core CPU can run 4 tasks in parallel. But only if the software is written to use them.
A bigger cache means more cache hits, fewer slow RAM trips. Even doubling the cache can noticeably boost performance for memory-heavy tasks.

numericals.q: A CPU runs at 2 GHz. How many cycles per second is that, in billions?
